text:
Ben K: running a 48h experiment to move some noisy GPU alerts from paging -> ticketing. goal is to cut late-night noise without losing actionable pages for real incidents. plan: only page when we see sustained cluster-level OOM spikes, otherwise auto-create tickets for follow-up. thoughts? :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Alex P: curious on the exact prometheus rule you want to change. will that affect dedicated fleets?

Ben K: good q. rule targets `fleet:gpu_oom_rate:sum` (cluster-level). current behavior: page on any single instance >1 OOM in 1m. new behavior: page if `sum(rate(gpu_oom_total[5m])) by (cluster) > 3` for `for: 5m`. otherwise fire a `severity: ticket` alert that escalates if it persists 30m.

Mira S: Agree with cluster aggregation. Also propose hysteresis so we don't flip pages on transient blips. e.g. require >3 for 5m to page, and require <1 for 10m to resolve.

Jamal: +1. Also recommend grouping_key: `{{cluster}}:{{region}}:{{gpu_type}}` so teams get a single ticket per affected pool instead of per-instance spam.

Ben K: here's the snippet I'll push to staging (psuedo):
```yaml
- alert: GPUOOMClusterHigh
  expr: sum(rate(gpu_oom_total[5m])) by (cluster) > 3
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "Cluster {{ $labels.cluster }} high GPU OOM rate"

- alert: GPUOOMClusterPersistent
  expr: sum(rate(gpu_oom_total[5m])) by (cluster) > 1
  for: 30m
  labels:
    severity: ticket
```

Mira S: Also add `mute_window` routing for non-prod clusters between 23:00-07:00 UTC. For prod keep paging 24/7.

Alex P: What about network-related flaps that look like OOMs? we should exclude nodes with recent `node_network_flap_total > 0` or at least annotate.

Ben K: good call. will annotate any correlated `node_network_flap` events and lower page priority.

Jamal: we should measure false-positive rate pre/post. propose metric: `alert:gpu_oom_pages_total{outcome="resolved_by_autoretry"}` vs `...{escalated="paged"}`. run for 2w.

deploy-bot: alert-config-change staged -> prometheus-staging at 2026-03-18T15:12:00Z :package:

Ben K: scheduling a quick 15m sync at 15:30 UTC to run through playbook and rollback plan. if no objections I'll flip this to prod after 48h of staging data. :calendar: :thumbsup:

Mira S: ack. pls post playbook link and rollback command in the thread.

Alex P: ack from me too. thanks for running the experiment.

Jamal: +1.

Ben K: posted playbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-oom-paging-experiment — rollback is `kubectl apply -f alerts/gpu-oom-original.yaml`

Mira S: one last thought — add a runbook step to check `slo:gpu_inference_latency` after change to ensure we didn't mask real perf regressions.

Ben K: will add. flipping to prod tentatively 2026-03-20T15:00:00Z if staging looks good.
